lectures.title: Showing a Loading Indicator & Sending Correct Data

cues.en: Now, sending a request like this is nice, but maybe we also want to give the user a little feedback
that we're sending a request and that we're waiting for their response.
For that, we can show a loading spinner or at least a loading text so we can add a new variable here
in our component where we say is loading.
And initially that is false.
But when we send the request right before we call fetch, we can set is loading to true and we only
want to change this once we're done.
So we want to change this here in the then block where we set is loading back to false, but also in
the error block.
Because even if we have an error, we're not waiting for the request anymore.
And here we could throw an alert.
Where we say saved data, though of course you might not really want to use an alert because that really
breaks the user experience in my opinion.
But here for demo purposes, let's do that as well so that we see that we reach this point here as well.
So with that, let's take advantage of the Isloading variable by checking whether Isloading is true.
And if it is true, you could show a loading spinner here or at least some text loading.
And maybe only show the full list after this loading is done.
So move that unordered list into the else block here.
Let's give this a try.
Back here, let's add sports.
And now you need to watch closely because Firebase is really fast and the response will be back in no
time.
But you see loading here and then thanks to the alert, was actually visible for quite some time because
the UI only updated after dismissing the alert.
But thereafter you see sports again and the same if we add cooking here, if we add cooking loading,
click okay, it's gone.
We see that.
So this is all working.
And on the backend we see that two new items was added were added sports again, huh?
And then here sports and cooking.
So actually our whole list was added here.
Well, the reason for that is that I am simply sending my full hobbies array here.
We could do that.
But actually I want to send the individual hobby which was added for that.
Of course, I simply have to use hobby input value as a value which we send here and it's up to you
what you want to store on the backend.
Do you want to send each hobby or always the full list?
So let's delete the hobbies on the backend here to start from scratch and let's give this another try.
Let's add sports here.
That seems to work.
Let's add cooking here.
And that also works.
And now here we actually see this was added in a different format because now we still have that unique
identifier, but then we don't have this nested array in there because we're not sending an array anymore.
But instead we simply have this string added next to that unique identifier.
And this, if you fetch it, will actually be a JavaScript object where the identifier is the property
name and that is the value.
Well, speaking of fetching, let's do that because right now if I reload this, our list is gone.
